name: Popups and interruptions
summary: Never interrupt the user: a popup, popover, modal, drawer, toast, coachmark, tour or announcement opens only as the direct result of an explicit user action, never on load, a timer, scroll, idle, exit intent, sign-in or a first visit. A timer the user set is their action. Two exceptions: information whose absence causes obvious damage, and a promotional popup for a free-plan user past 14 days.
highlights: Opens only from an explicit user action on that screen
Never on load, timer, scroll, idle, exit intent, sign-in or first visit
A timer the user set (a slide timer, Time's up) is their action
Two exceptions: obvious damage, and a promotion after 14 days on free
lead: Every unsolicited popup is an interruption. Never interrupt the user unless missing the information would cause them obvious damage. An overlay opens only because the user asked for it: a click, tap, key press or submit on the thing it belongs to, or a hover or focus on a tooltip's trigger. Information that would otherwise be announced in a popup goes in the page, where the user meets it. The rule judges what a change adds; it never asks to change or remove a feature that already ships. Which surface to use is the Overlays guideline's call.

skillRef.note: This page is the human-readable source of the rule; usability U11 in anti-slop/criteria.json is its check. The overlay surfaces themselves are in the overlays guideline.

rules.rule: A popup, popover, modal, drawer, toast, coachmark, product tour or announcement opens only as the direct result of an explicit user action on that screen: a click, tap, key press or submit on the thing it belongs to (for a tooltip, a hover or focus on its trigger).

Nothing opens by itself: not on page load, on a timer, on scroll, when idle, on exit intent, after sign-in or on a first visit, and never to announce a feature or ask for a rating, survey or upgrade. Put that information in the page where the user will meet it.

A timer the user set is their own action: when a slide timer the presenter set runs out and the presenting screen closes submissions and shows Time's up, or a countdown the user started ends, that is the consequence of their setting, not an uninvited popup.

Two exceptions only: (1) information that, if missed, would cause the user obvious damage (unsaved work about to be lost, a session about to expire, a failed payment that will cut access); (2) a promotional popup shown to a free-plan user who signed up more than 14 days ago.
The rule judges what a change adds; it never asks to change or remove an existing feature.

reuseNote: Doc-only rule. It ships no component: the overlay surfaces are the overlays guideline's, and usability U11 in anti-slop/criteria.json is the check.
